 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of Chandu H.N was died in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 11.07.2023 at about 11.50pm.

2. The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
On 11.07.2023 at about 11.50pm the deceased pillion rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-3489, Mohan Kumar was the rider of the motorcycle, proceeding from nice road towards Sunkadakatte with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, without observing any traffic rules, at Opp.
Vivo Mobile Show Room, Anjananagar, Magadi Main Road, Bengaluru city, rider lost control over the motorcycle and dashed center maiden electric Pole.
As a result of the forced impact, the deceased and the rider were thrown out, fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
As a result both rider & pillion rider were succumbed to the injuries on spot.
Thereafter body was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and post mortem was conducted on 12.07.2023, body was handed over to the petitioners.
Petitioners performed funeral obsequies by spending Rs.1,00,000/- towards transpiration of dead body and funeral expenses.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that the deceased was aged about 21 years, hale and healthy, working as a Writer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and entire amount contributed to the maintenance of his family.
Due to the sudden and unnatural death, petitioners undergoing great mental shock and mental agony.
They are put to great financial difficulties and hardship for his livelihood.

The accident was occurred due o the negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-3489 and Kamaksipalya Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.190/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 338 & 304(a) of the IPC against the rider of the said offending vehicle rider.
The 1 st respondent being the Insurer and 2nd respondent being the RC owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5. The respondent No.1 has filed objections by denying the entire averments made in the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Respondent No.2 in respect of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-3489.
It has denied that the deceased died due to injuries suffered by him in the Road Traffic Accident.
It has denied the involvement of the motorcycle in the accident.
Further stated that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid driving license as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also denied the expenses towards funeral etc.,
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and highly excessive.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
6. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are arises for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri.Chandu H.N.?
Issue No.2:

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Chandu H.N., had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occured on 11.07.2023 at about 11.50p.m, opposite Vivo mobile showroom, Magadi Main Road, Anjananagara, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP- 3489 as alleged?
Issue No.3: Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, what amount and from whom?
Issue No.4: What order or Award?

11. The PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
In the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated the offending motorcycle was belonged to his uncle.
The complaint was lodged by him.
One Mohan was riding the motorcycle.
Further admitted that both rider and pillion rider were not wearing the helmet as on the date of accident.
He further denied other suggestions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

12. To prove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased, they have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Cards of the petitioners and the deceased and their parents, Death Certificate of deceased's father and mother and family Ration Card at Exs.P.9 to 13.
Ex.P.6 Inquest mahazar also shows the names and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
13. The petitioners have totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the deceased and offending vehicle's rider.
It is no doubt the police have submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle after thorough investigation.

The sketch appended to spot mahazar indicates that the deceased was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HP-3489 as a pillion rider and the motorcycle was driven by the rider Mohan with high speed towards Magadi Road, Byadarahalli and lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the Road center median and caused the accident.
The Sketch further depicts that the motorcycle proceeding towards Magadi Road and the accident spot is on the middle of the Road at Center Median.
The sketch clearly depicts that the offending vehicle was moving towards Magadi Road.
The oral evidence of the petitioners have coupled with documentary evidence.

14. It is the specific case of the insurer that the ride3r and the deceased were in the intoxicant condition at the time of the accident and the pillion rider has also contributed to accident in question.

The petitioner has placed the post mortem report marked at Ex.P7, it indicates that "blood is collected, preserved, packed, labeled, sealed and handed over to the concerned police along with same for detection of alcohol levels at Forensic Science Laboratory."
The petitioners have not placed the FSL report throughout the proceedings.
However, the insurer has produced the FSL Report of deceased rider of the bike marked at Ex.R3.

This document depicts the final opinion of the expert as follows: "On perusal of the Post Mortem findings, FSL report and your requisition letter, I am of the opinion that "cause of death remains the same i.e., death is due to head injury sustained, however the deceased had consumed Ethyl Alcohol (43.01mg/100ml) prior to death."

As per this document it is mentioned that "quantum of Ethyl Alcohol in Article No.2 = 43.01mg/100ml of blood sample of Mohan Kumar M. Our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held in a case of 1Kamala Bai v.
Divisional Manager, K.S.R.T.C., - Merely because a person had consumed alcohol, it cannot be said that the accident has occurred due to his negligence.
As I referred above the police have submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offenses punishable under section 185 of Motor Vehicle.
To rebut the same no cogent evidence is placed by the petitioners.

18. As per the police documents, the deceased rider was in intoxicant stage, so, it can be presumed that the rider of the motorcycle was unable to ride his vehicle consuming with alcohol and he would have not taken care of front going/standing vehicle/median while riding his motorcycle.

Therefore,
the alleged accident was occurred due to negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, issue Nos.1 and 2 are held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3: The Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 being the grand mother and younger brother of the deceased.
It is the contention of the petitioners that the deceased was doing Writer work and earning of Rs.20,000/- Per month.
The petitioner No.2 has reiterated the same in the chief examination affidavit.
But the petitioners have not placed any material worth in this regard.
As per the claim petition the age of the deceased was 21 years.

The Aadhar Card of the deceased and online copy of Ration Card/change of address/member details receipt at Exs.P.9 & 13 discloses that the date of birth of the deceased is 12.11.2002, as such, the age was 20 years.
Therefore, the age of the deceased will be considered as 20 years as on the date of his death.
As I mentioned above, the petitioners have not placed any material worth to show the exact income of the deceased.

So,
considering the nature of work and year of accident, the chart prepared, furnished by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru is taken in to consideration, the notional income of Rs.16,000/-pm is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in a judgment reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held in aragraph No.21 that 3 Magma General Insurance Co. sentences.text: One of these heads is Loss of Consortium.

In legal parlance Consortium is a compendious term which encompasses Spousal Consortium;
Parental consortium and filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company,
care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse."

21 1 "Spousal Consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of Company, Society, co operation,
affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation"
21 2
"Parental Consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."13,50,180
21 3 " Filial Consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of the Child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock, agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.

Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit."
22.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world over have recognized that the value of a Child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore, permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.

The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child".
24.
The Petitioners are the grandmother and brother.
They are not entitled to any compensation under any heads as aforesaid.
25. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

The next question is the liability to pay the said compensation.
As I referred above the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle and has also contributed to the alleged accident.
The insurer has proved that the rider of the offending bike was in intoxicant stage while riding the bike.
The charge sheet also filed against the rider of the offending motorcycle with consuming alcohol.
It is not in dispute that the insurance was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

27. APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION:
The claimants No.1 & 2 being grandmother and younger brother of the deceased.
Hence, they are entitled for 60:40 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.

On deposit of compensation, the petitioners are entitled to withdraw 50% of their share and remaining share shall be invested as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years on proper identification.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 partly in Affirmative.
28. Issue No.4:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.1.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimants under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation tune of Rs.24,55,200/- (Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs Fifty Five Thousand Two Hundred Only) together interest @ 6%pa from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment, after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
The petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are entitled for 60:40 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
